description: A model of the four-transistor Big Muff Pi fuzz of 1976: a booster, two diode-clipped stages, the passive scooped tone network and a recovery stage, one pedal per channel

params.text: Sets what a 5V signal in Rack arrives as at the pedal's input, 0.01V to 3V; it is not a pedal control and it exists because Rack runs some 25dB hotter than a guitar pickup
Sets how hard the clipping pair is driven, 0% to 100%; it is a level going into the stages rather than a threshold, which is why there is no clean setting
Walks the clipping stages' operating point off centre, ±100%, for the starved, gated, lopsided sound; it is not a pedal control
Sweeps the passive tone network from bass to treble; it is two branches with a notch between them rather than a tilt
Fills the tone network's scooped middle back in, 0% to 100%; it is not a pedal control

inputs.text: The signal to distort, one pedal per channel of a polyphonic cable
Added to the sustain knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the tone knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the volume knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it

outputs.text: The fuzz, on as many channels as the input carries

notes: the gain trimmer is the one control with no counterpart on the pedal. Its default of about 0.13V is a hot guitar, and turning it up walks the pedal into where a modular signal would put it.
the lamps show clipping and output level.
menu: Clipping diodes — which pair clips the two stages: Silicon 1N4148 (stock), Germanium (earlier, softer), LED (louder, cleaner) or Lifted (no diodes)
